Empirical Research Plan – Expanding Access to Group-Lending Microcredit in Hyderabad, India
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

1. IDENTIFICATION STRATEGY  
   • Primary design: Difference-in-Differences (DID) at the neighbourhood (basti) × time level.  
   • Extensions: (i) Event-study specification to inspect dynamic effects and pre-trends, (ii) 2-stage least squares (2SLS) that uses Spandana branch opening as an instrument for actual borrowing to obtain Treatment-on-the-Treated (TOT) effects.  
   Rationale: 52 of 104 bastis receive the programme between the 2005 baseline and the two follow-up surveys. The staggered roll-out provides plausibly exogenous temporal and spatial variation that can be leveraged with DID; the event study sharpens the parallel-trend test; the IV converts “offer” into “take-up”.

2. TREATMENT AND CONTROL  
   • Treatment indicator (Offer/ITT):  
     Treat_nbht_it = 1 if basti i is served by a Spandana branch that opened ≤ 6 months before survey t, 0 otherwise.  
   • Control group: Bastis with no Spandana branch by survey date t.  
   • Timing: Exact month of each branch opening is known (2006–2007). Survey dates are known.  
   • Secondary treatment (Borrow/TOT):  
     Borrow_hht = 1 if household has an outstanding Spandana loan at survey t. 1st-stage instrument = Treat_nbht_it.  
   • Sample: All households that satisfy Spandana’s eligibility rules at baseline to keep treatment and control pools comparable (woman 18–55, resident ≥3 yrs).  
   Note: No RDD is feasible because there is no explicit running variable with a sharp threshold.

3. KEY IDENTIFYING ASSUMPTIONS  
   A1. Parallel Trends – In the absence of Spandana, treated and control bastis would have evolved similarly. Plausible because: (i) Spandana expressed “indifference” across the 104 eligible bastis; (ii) 2005 baseline predates any MFI presence; (iii) high-frequency city-wide shocks (GDP growth, inflation) hit all bastis.  
   A2. Stable Unit Treatment Value (No Spillovers) – Entry in a treated basti does not directly change outcomes in control bastis. Reasonable: group-lending requires weekly physical meetings; distance/friction costs limit cross-basti borrowing. We will check by dropping control bastis within 1 km of treated ones.  
   A3. No Differential Attrition – Survey re-contact is ≈ 90%; attrition is not systematically related to treatment once covariates are conditioned on. We will test by regressing attrition on treatment.  
   A4. Exogeneity of Instrument (for IV) – Branch opening affects outcomes only through borrowing, conditional on basti and time fixed effects. Given Spandana’s business-driven but coarse targeting and absence of additional services, exclusion is plausible.  

4. THREATS TO IDENTIFICATION & MITIGATION  
   T1. Pre-existing Trend Differences  
       • Test: Event-study coefficients for years −2/−1 should be ≈ 0.  
       • Mitigate: Add basti-specific linear trends; robustness to removing bastis with large pre-trend deviations.  
   T2. Contamination by Other MFIs  
       • Strategy: Collect data on entry dates of other MFIs; include an “OtherMFI_it” dummy; run spec that excludes periods after other MFI entry.  
   T3. Selective Household Attrition  
       • Strategy: Inverse-probability weighting using baseline covariates that predict survey retention; bounding exercise (Lee bounds).  

5. R CODE OUTLINE
```r
# 0. Packages
library(data.table)   # fast manipulation
library(fixest)       # high-dim FE & IV
library(ggplot2)      # event-study plot
library(WeightIt)     # attrition weights (robustness)

# 1. Load data
hh05  <- fread("baseline_2005.csv")      # baseline
hh07  <- fread("endline_2007.csv")       # 15-18 months after entry
hh10  <- fread("endline_2010.csv")       # 3–4 years after entry
branches <- fread("spandana_branches.csv")  # basti_id, open_month

# 2. Stack surveys into long panel
allsurv <- rbindlist(list(hh05, hh07, hh10), fill = TRUE)
allsurv[, survey_year := year(survey_date)]

# 3. Construct treatment variables
## Merge branch info
allsurv <- merge(allsurv, branches, by = "basti_id", all.x = TRUE)

## Treatment offer
allsurv[, treat_offer := as.integer(open_month <= survey_month - 6)]

## Borrow (any Spandana loan)
allsurv[, borrow := as.integer(outstanding_spandana_loan > 0)]

# 4. Controls
baseline_demo <- c("hh_size", "female_head", "edu_head", "scst", "log_assets05")

# 5. Main DID regression – Intent-to-Treat
did_spec <- feols(outcome ~ treat_offer + i(survey_year) + baseline_demo | basti_id + survey_date,
                  cluster = ~basti_id, data = allsurv)

# 6. 2-stage least squares – Treatment-on-the-Treated
iv_spec <- feols(outcome ~ 1 | basti_id + survey_date | borrow ~ treat_offer,
                 cluster = ~basti_id, data = allsurv)

# 7. Event-study (relative time in years)
allsurv[, rel_year := survey_year - floor(open_month/12)]
evt <- feols(outcome ~ i(rel_year, ref = -1) | basti_id + survey_year,
             cluster = ~basti_id, data = allsurv[abs(rel_year) <= 4])

# 8. Robustness: drop controls within 1 km of treated bastis
close_pairs <- fread("neighbor_pairs_1km.csv")  # basti_id, close_to_treated
robust_spec <- feols(outcome ~ treat_offer | basti_id + survey_date,
                     cluster = ~basti_id,
                     data = merge(allsurv, close_pairs)[close_to_treated == 0])
```

6. EXPECTED RESULTS  
   Theory predicts heterogeneous but modest effects. Prior expectations:  
   • Borrowing: +20 pp in treated vs control.  
   • Business creation: +6 pp; profits roughly flat (reallocation from wage to self-employment).  
   • Consumption: little change in nondurables; +0–3 % in durables; no effect on temptation goods.  
   • Education/Health: essentially 0.  
   • Women’s decision-making index: +0.05 SD.  
   Persistence: effects on borrowing and business assets should attenuate but stay positive after 3 years; consumption effects likely fade.

7. VALIDITY CHECKLIST SELF-ASSESSMENT (DID)  
   C1. Common trends pre-treatment                      1  
   C2. No spillovers / SUTVA                             0.5 (some geographic leak possible)  
   C3. No differential composition changes               0.8  
   C4. Exogenous treatment timing                        0.7  
   C5. Accurate measurement of treatment & outcomes      1  
   Overall ≈ 4.0 / 5 → reasonable internal validity.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
